record.trigger: A component requirement assigns a binary command by operating mode and threshold bands, and explicitly says to hold the command within hysteresis bands.
record.principle: Preserve mode guards, exact interval boundaries, and command history together when translating hysteresis requirements into architecture, contracts, implementation, proof obligations, and tests.
record.semantic_choice: Interpret 'hold alarm control' as equality to the previous emitted command. Interpret 'below' and 'above' strictly and retain the stated inclusive boundaries. Apply temperature cases only in NORMAL mode; initialization, INIT, and FAILED retain their separate assignments.
record.structural_placement: The command-producing thread owns the output and private command history. Attach its behavioral contract there. Preserve process forwarding connections and system wiring; the mode manager supplies mode and the interface manager supplies thresholds.
record.repair_gate: Before accepting a proposed repair, require interface preservation, traceability of every changed guard or assignment, initialization and history-update reasoning, interval coverage and overlap analysis, and boundary/sequence tests. Do not weaken guards, remove cases, or add input assumptions merely to discharge an obligation. Missing prerequisites leave application unresolved.
prerequisites: The target explicitly requires the same mode-gated binary hysteresis semantics; lexical similarity alone is insufficient.
Output ownership, input sampling, initialization, and the meaning of the previous emitted command are established.
Thresholds and hysteresis width have compatible units and representable arithmetic; the supported input domain and threshold ordering are established.
Any stronger spacing assumption, such as a nonempty reset band, must come from the target requirements rather than this rule.
Target mode mappings, initial output, and mode overrides are established independently before instantiation.
exclusions: Stateless range alarms that specify an unconditional reset throughout the range.
Timed debounce, timeout, filtering, or rate-dependent hysteresis.
Inference of sensor-validity guards or end-to-end latency from the periodic dispatch declaration.
Changes to existing ports, types, connections, scheduling declarations, or unrelated component behavior.

parameters.constraints: Use existing interfaces, a common measurement scale, and the established input domain.

parameters.name: h
parameters.constraints: Positive and requirement-backed; the observed alarm uses 1 [s32] in degrees-field arithmetic. Do not infer a physical temperature unit.

parameters.name: q, p
parameters.role: Emitted command and private prior-command state
parameters.constraints: Use the existing binary command type; initialize p consistently with the initial emitted command and update it after every emission.

parameters.name: mode
parameters.constraints: Preserve existing enumerations and source-backed mode assignments.

dependencies: Existing mode producer and threshold producer contracts
Target execution semantics for persistent state and sampled inputs
Target numeric types and arithmetic semantics
preserved_obligations: Architecture: retain all source interfaces, forwarding connections, ownership boundaries, and scheduling declarations.
Contract: retain source initialization, mode-specific outputs, strict outside-range tests, inclusive reset boundaries, and prior-command equality in both hysteresis bands.
Implementation: initialize history consistently, compute from pre-update history, emit the required command, then record that command, including emissions in overriding modes.

Proof: establish initialization and inductive correspondence between history and the previous emitted command; establish each guarded implication and consistent coverage over the supported input domain.
Proof: check arithmetic representability and every overlapping interval; do not assume cases are disjoint or silently impose branch priority.
Testing: exercise each mode, both prior commands, exact boundaries L, L+h, U-h, U, representable neighboring values, and multi-dispatch entry/hold/reset sequences.
Testing: exercise mode transitions and supported threshold changes to expose stale-history errors.
Repair: preserve unrelated guarantees and interfaces, localize changes to the owning behavior and its supporting verification artifacts, and repeat affected checks.

counterexample.scenario: In NORMAL mode with L=97, U=103, h=1 and previous command On, the sampled temperature becomes exactly 97.
counterexample.expected_difference: This rule requires On to be retained because 97 lies in the lower hold band. A stateless implementation that emits Off whenever L <= x <= U violates that obligation. If the target explicitly requires that stateless reset behavior, this rule does not apply.

record.notes: Observed: Manage_Alarm_i declares lastCmd, initializes alarm_control to Off, and supplies mode-gated outside-range, hold-band, reset-band, and FAILED cases. It does not supply executable history initialization or updates. Its period is 1000 ms. Proposed: the implementation, proof, testing, and repair obligations above are inferred requirements for preserving those cases, not observed development results. No validation implementation or held-out component is supplied. Source references and hashes await assignment by the trusted controller.
source_english_patterns: If mode NORMAL and current temperature is inside the lower hysteresis band then hold alarm control
If mode NORMAL and current temperature is inside the upper hysteresis band then hold alarm control
If mode NORMAL and current temperature is inside the reset band then alarm control is Off
positive_paraphrases: While operating normally, retain the previous command in either hysteresis band.
Outside the permitted range activate the alarm; reset it within the inner band, subject to the stated mode guards.
misleading_near_matches: Turn the alarm off whenever the temperature returns anywhere inside the range.
Hold the alarm for one second after a threshold crossing.
Turn the alarm on at or below the lower threshold.

semantic_roles.actor: The thread owning the binary command output
semantic_roles.condition: Current sampled mode and threshold interval, with prior command required for hold cases
semantic_roles.effect: Emit the mode override, activate outside the range, reset in the inner band, or retain the prior command
semantic_roles.quantification: Every applicable compute dispatch over the established input domain
semantic_roles.temporal_scope: Initialization followed by successive command emissions; no additional wall-clock guarantee inferred
semantic_roles.state_dependency: Hold compares the new output to the previous emitted command, not to an already updated history variable
semantic_roles.units_and_boundaries: Preserve strict outside inequalities, half-open hold bands, and closed reset band; verify target units and arithmetic

record.formal_output_pattern: ABSTRACT transition relation, not executable GUMBO: initialize q := Off and p := Off. For each compute dispatch, let p_pre be the previous emitted command. Require (mode=INIT => q=Off); (mode=FAILED => q=On); (mode=NORMAL and (x<L or x>U) => q=On); (mode=NORMAL and ((L<=x and x<L+h) or (U-h<x and x<=U)) => q=p_pre); (mode=NORMAL and L+h<=x and x<=U-h => q=Off). After emitting q, set p_post := q. All implications are simultaneous obligations; demonstrate coverage and compatibility under established domain constraints. Instantiate On with the existing source literal Onn.

Owning implementation's initialization and compute behavior

required_baseline: Existing interfaces, wiring, scheduling declarations, and unrelated guarantees
Target requirements for mode behavior, interval boundaries, and initialization
Established numeric domain and execution semantics
